subject: Procurement & commercial path options — AWS/GCP marketplace vs PO (post-call recap)
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <procurement@cloudwave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: procurement & commercial path options (AWS/GCP Marketplace vs PO)

Hi Asha — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so your procurement and finance teams have clarity: 

Summary of what we heard:
- CloudWave is interested in Redwood for high-throughput inference in production for the MediaGen product line.
- Procurement preference: leaning toward formal PO / invoice route but want to evaluate AWS Marketplace for simpler entitlement and consolidation with other cloud vendors.
- Key constraints: corporate T&C review by week of Nov 29, needs SOC 2 evidence and data residency notes, and they want to avoid manual invoicing overhead where possible.

Commercial paths we discussed (pros/cons):
1) Direct PO / Net-30 invoice (preferred by CloudWave finance) — fastest to align contract terms, supports consolidated billing, requires Redwood billing ops to accept PO and map invoice codes.
2) AWS / GCP Marketplace listing — smoother procurement for CloudWave Procurement (same bill run) and easier procurement approvals, but adds listing lead time (we estimated 3–5 weeks) and marketplace cut / entitlements differences.
3) Credit card / corporate card pilot — quickest to start (low friction) but not scalable for central finance and will likely be rejected for enterprise spend.

Proposed next steps (action owners):
- Redwood (Karthik): circulate a short procurement checklist and SOW for review by EOD 11/18. (attached: Redwood_Marketplace_Procure_Checklist.pdf, Redwood_SOW_v1.docx)
- CloudWave (Asha): confirm whether you want us to prioritize Marketplace onboarding vs. PO-ing the first term. If PO, send preferred PO template and billing contact.
- Redwood (Ben): stand up an initial invoice/PO flow and confirm tax / remit details; provide account code mapping.
- Redwood (Marissa): capture any marketplace technical listing questions (IAM roles, entitlement mapping, minimum supported instance types).

Open questions we flagged:
- Who owns signing on CloudWave side (legal vs procurement)?
- Will CloudWave require a separate reseller agreement for marketplace purchases?
- Any data residency or logging export requirements beyond SOC 2?

I’ve CC’d Marissa (SE) and Ben (Billing) to help close the technical and billing gaps. If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute procurement-only call with your finance team early next week.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the concise recap. Helpful. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Preferred commercial path: Our finance team prefers PO / invoice for any multi-month committed spend. Marketplace would be our secondary choice if the listing supports consolidated enterprise billing and we can get the same contractual terms (SLA, termination, data controls).

2) Timing & approvals: Our legal team is out on the 24th–26th; we need paperwork before Nov 29 to make a Dec 1 service start realistic. SOC 2 + a short description of data handling (where logs are stored and retention) will be required for the review packet.

3) Contacts:
- Procurement: Asha Patel (procurement@cloudwave.com) — I will own PO issuance.
- Finance AP: Tom Nguyen (tom.nguyen@cloudwave.com) — will confirm remit / account codes once I confirm approach.

Next step for us: please send the PO template we should expect (or your invoice remit instructions) and any marketplace listing estimated timeline. If Marketplace onboarding is >3 weeks we will likely proceed with a PO for the initial term and evaluate moving to Marketplace for renewals.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll circulate to legal now and get back with which path we want to lock.

Best,

Thanks Karthik and Asha — quick technical/ops notes on Marketplace vs direct PO so CloudWave can weigh risk/effort: 

Marketplace (AWS/GCP) implications:
- Onboarding timeline: 3–5 weeks to get listing, test entitlements, and finalize pricing tiers. If CloudWave wants co-term billing with existing AWS spend, we can request Private Offers, but that requires an additional procurement step from AWS side.
- Entitlements: Marketplace uses SKU-based entitlements; mapping from Redwood account IDs to CloudWave IAM principals typically takes one small integration task (we provide an entitlement script).
- Support & SLAs: Marketplace purchases can still be covered by Redwood SLAs; we just need to ensure the SKU terms match the contract (we can surface that in the Private Offer).
- Data/access: no change to data residency; runtime logs live in our cloud region (we'll include a short excerpt for legal).

If you go straight to PO / invoice:
- Ben will need the PO template and company remit details (address, tax id, AP contact).
- We can attach a 30-day termination SOW for initial term to speed sign-off (attached SOW).

Attachments: Redwood_Marketplace_Procure_Checklist.pdf (high level checklist for marketplace vs PO onboarding).

Suggested short milestone plan (if CloudWave wants both paths open):
1) Week 0 (today): Redwood sends SOW + procurement checklist (done).
2) Week 1: CloudWave confirms path (PO vs Marketplace) and sends PO template / AP contact.
3) Week 1–3: If Marketplace chosen, Redwood submits listing and requests Private Offer; if PO chosen, finance exchanges PO and Redwood issues invoice.

Happy to jump on a short call with your AP/legal if that speeds decisions.
—Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
